description: PROBE 1-c (9b, bean cywi): derive-or-refute the [Z>N] proton-excess gate of model M3 from the Phase-5q interface algebra. Exact mirror decomposition gap = asym + swap + mirror (identity ≤1e-30); gate exact ⟺ swap+mirror = 0. At A=3 the cancellation holds to −0.0337 (= res_M3(³He) − res_M3(T), identity), but the swap term decays geometrically with A (derived: all f ∈ (0,1) at q₀) while the AME mirror term stays O(0.4): at ⁷Li/⁷Be swap+mirror = +0.394. VERDICT: gate-as-derived-rule REFUTED scope-(a); A=3 near-match retained with stated residual. Exploratory; NOT wired; no new constants.

verdict.question: is the [Z>N] proton-excess gate of M3 a derived consequence of the Phase-5q interface algebra, or an A=3 coincidence?
verdict.gate_statement: gate exact ⟺ swap + mirror = 0, where swap is the interface-sign-swap term (closed form) and mirror is the AME mirror-binding ratio (experimental); identically res_M3(p-rich) − res_M3(n-rich) = −(swap + mirror)
verdict.tier: REFUTED as a generic derived rule — scope (a) ONLY; NEAR-MATCH retained at A=3 with exact stated residual
verdict.scope_a_statement: The interface algebra, ALONE, does not derive the [Z>N] gate: the swap term it supplies decays geometrically with A (−0.938 → −0.117 → −0.0167 at A=3/5/7; derived from 0 < f < 1 at q₀), while the AME mirror term it must cancel stays O(0.4) (+0.904 / +0.438 / +0.410). The A=3 cancellation (residual −0.0337) is a numerical coincidence of that one pair; at ⁷Li/⁷Be the same combination is +0.394. This constrains the gate-as-rule reading only — it does NOT exclude the trace asymmetry κ from a larger closure, and the A=3 near-match stands with its residual stated (no proved invariant; scope-(b) NOT claimed).
verdict.A3_status: M3 remains NEAR-MATCH at A=3: residuals D +0.011 / T +0.067 / ³He +0.033 / ⁴He −0.272; the ³He collapse works exactly because swap+mirror = −0.0337 ≈ 0 there
caveats: A=5 pair (⁵He/⁵Li) is particle-unstable — corroborating only; A=7 (⁷Li/⁷Be) is the clean bound-pair test
